title: A wanderer dancing the dance of stars and space
caption: The star-forming ring of NGC 1097, imaged by the Hubble Space Telescope
celestial: NGC 1097 · constellation Fornax · about 65 million light-years away (source figure)

recognition.text: ESA/Hubble Picture of the Week (an editorial selection, not an audience score).

story: A bright ring of star formation surrounds the core of NGC 1097, a barred spiral galaxy, in this Hubble image. The galaxy's larger structure is barely visible here; its comparatively dim spiral arms loop loosely around the centre and reach beyond the frame. NGC 1097 is a face-on galaxy lying 45 million light-years away in the southern constellation Fornax, the Furnace.

It is a Seyfert galaxy. At its centre, a supermassive black hole 100 million times the Sun's mass is slowly drawing in the matter around it, and the region right beside it shines strongly with radiation from that infalling material. The ring, about 5000 light-years across, is packed with new stars, fed by material flowing toward the galaxy's central bar, and its star-forming regions glow with ionised hydrogen.
Supernova hunters like this galaxy too: three supernovae went off here in an 11-year span beginning in 1992.
scale: Using the source's listed field of view (3.41 x 2.24 arcminutes) and distance (65 million light years), the frame spans roughly 64,000 × 42,000 light-years. Its light set out about 65 million years before reaching the telescope.

understand.summary: Hubble's Advanced Camera for Surveys observed through a hydrogen-alpha filter and a near-infrared filter; the colour mapping isn't published.
understand.eye: The near-infrared filter records light the eye cannot see, and the hydrogen-alpha filter isolates the glow of ionised hydrogen.

explore: NGC 1097 has two small companions outside this frame: NGC 1097A, an elliptical orbiting 42 000 light-years from the centre, and a dwarf called NGC 1097B. Astronomers have signs that NGC 1097 and NGC 1097A interacted in the past. A version of this image was entered in Hubble's Hidden Treasures competition by Eedresha Sturdivant.
alt: The centre of a barred spiral galaxy, with a bright ring of star-forming regions around its core.
